item.title: Kinds of Numbers: A Map from Natural to Complex
item.author: hari@dasarpai.com (Dr. Hari Thapliyaal)
item.description:
Kinds of Numbers
#

Nested sets from counting to the complex plane, plus bases and computer formats
#

Natural → integer → rational → real → complex is the main ladder. Each step adds numbers the previous step could not hold.

Kind Symbol (usual) One-line idea Example
Natural $\mathbb{N}$ Counting sizes $1, 2, 3, \ldots$
Whole — Natural plus zero $0, 1, 2, \ldots$
Integer $\mathbb{Z}$ Whole numbers and negatives $-3, 0, 7$
Rational $\mathbb{Q}$ Ratio of two integers $\tfrac{3}{4}$, $-2$, $0.125$
Irrational (inside $\mathbb{R}$) Real, not any exact fraction $\sqrt{2}$, $\pi$
Real $\mathbb{R}$ Points on the number line $-1.5$, $e$, $\sqrt{5}$
Imaginary — Real multiple of $i$ $3i$, $-i$
Complex $\mathbb{C}$ Real part plus imaginary part $2 + 3i$

Two phrases sound alike but mean different things:

  • Kinds of numbers — which set a value belongs to ($\mathbb{Q}$, $\mathbb{R}$, …).
  • Positional number system — how you write a value in a base (decimal, binary, hex).

This article maps the sets first, then points at bases and floating-point formats data work uses every day.

For symbols and operators used with these numbers, see Grammar of Mathematics: Operators, Functions, Relations, and Symbols.
